articles.title: Miami Reportedly Switching Back to Nike from Adidas as Primary Apparel Provider for Uniforms, More
articles.summary: Miami is reportedly reuniting with Nike after more than a decade with Adidas as the school's main apparel provider.
articles.body:
Miami is reportedly reuniting with Nike after more than a decade with Adidas as the school's main apparel provider.

The university and Nike have agreed to a 10-year contract worth more than $200 million starting with the 2027 football season, according to Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald.

Fanbases That Should be Worried after Week 2 😨

Miami agreed to a 12-year deal reportedly worth more than $90 million with Adidas in 2015.

Prior to that contract, which expires June 30, 2027, Miami had been signed since 1987 with Nike.

That previous contract with Nike made Miami the first school to sign with a retailer providing apparel for all sports, per Matt Porter of the Palm Beach Post.

Miami will now resume that partnership for a 28th year after Adidas fell short of matching Nike's terms in its counteroffer, per Jackson.

According to Jackson, the Nike deal is worth around $20 million annually, including around $13 million in cash with the remaining value in apparel.

Miami's previous deal with Adidas was worth about $6.5 million in annual cash in addition to apparel, per Jackson. Adidas had also partnered with local high schools to provide uniforms and equipment to students in Miami-Dade County.

The news comes shortly after Adidas announced it had signed star Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney to an NIL deal.

Nike will now resume its partnership with Miami amid shifts in the collegiate apparel landscape that saw the brand parts ways with Penn State.

The Nittany Lions wore Nike gear for 33 years before the school announced it would switch to Adidas ahead of the 2026 season in a 10-year deal reportedly worth around $300 million.

Nike also parted ways this season with Tennessee, which began a new ten-year partnership with Adidas in July.

Miami started out what will now be its final season in Adidas uniforms with wins at Stanford and against visiting Florida A&M. The Hurricanes are preparing to face their first ACC opponent of the season with a Friday matchup at Wake Forest.

articles.title: El Madrid estudia el caso JJ Gabriel
articles.standfirst: El talento inglés de 15 años quiere dejar el United, con el club blanco muy atento a su situación
articles.summary: El talento inglés de 15 años quiere dejar el United, con el club blanco muy atento a su situación
articles.body: El caso JJ Gabriel llega a Madrid. El club blanco estudia la compleja situación del joven futbolista del Manchester United, club que quiere abandonar, descontento con la gestión de su aún cortísima carrera por parte del club de Old Trafford. El club blanco no está solo a la hora de monitorizar la situación de este extremo izquierdo de tan sólo 15 años (cumplirá 16 en octubre) al que el Inglaterra consideran el gran talento de sus categorías inferiores. El apodo de 'Kid Messi' (El niño Messi), no parece haber pesado en la corta pero espectacular carrera de JJ Gabriel, que atesora todo tipo de récords en el fútbol inglés de cantera. Entre ellos, el hat-trick al Sabah en la primera jornada de la Youth League, que se jugó la pasada semana, un hito más para un jugador internacional en todas las categorías inferiores de los Three Lions, incluyendo la sub 18 pese a sus 15 años. El pasado verano, de hecho, jugó ocho minutos con el primer equipo del ManU en un amistoso ante el Atlético de Madrid en Estocolmo. Pese al vértigo de su incipiente carrera, el jugador, según la prensa inglesa, ha pedido salir del United, descontento por su falta de oportunidades en el primer equipo. Como trasfondo de la situación, la comidilla futbolística de Inglaterra en los dos últimos días, la influencia de su padre, el exfutbolista irlandés Joe O’Cearuill, que desde su retirada se centró en diseñar la carrera futbolística de su hijo, que fue incluso objeto de una pugna entre Nike y Adidas por su patrocinio, con triunfo final de la marca americana. La situación, pese a todo, no es sencilla. El Madrid está estudiando todas las aristas de un asunto que puede ser espinoso, para entrar en una pelea en la que no estaría solo. Junto a él aparecen el resto de los grandes de Europa, desde el Barça hasta el PSG, pasando por el Bayern, el City o el Chelsea. Eso sin olvidar a un United que no se resigna a perder al que muchos consideran el mejor proyecto de canterano que ha asomado por Carrington en las últimas décadas. El Madrid es perfectamente conocedor de todas las circunstancias que rodean el caso de Gabriel. Consciente de las dificultades, pero recabando información antes de lanzarse a la ofensiva con todas las cartas en la mano.

articles.title: El chollo del Oviedo es Pablo Sáenz
articles.standfirst: El extremo llegó libre este verano tras meses de seguimiento y su impacto fue inmediato: 2 goles y una cláusula de 6 millones en Segunda
articles.summary: El extremo llegó libre este verano tras meses de seguimiento y su impacto fue inmediato: 2 goles y una cláusula de 6 millones en Segunda
articles.body: El Real Oviedo encontró en Pablo Sáenz una oportunidad de mercado que empieza a adquirir todavía más valor sobre el césped. El navarro llegó libre este verano, firmó hasta 2028 y ya suma dos goles en el arranque de temporada, además de haber estrellado dos disparos en los palos. Su rendimiento le ha valido también el premio Mahou 5 Estrellas al mejor jugador azul del mes de agosto. La operación llevaba tiempo cocinándose. El Oviedo comenzó a seguir de cerca a Sáenz durante su cesión en el Albacete, donde marcó cinco goles en la segunda vuelta. Su regreso al Granada no terminó de devolverle el protagonismo esperado y, con apenas un año de contrato por delante, su futuro empezó a alejarse de Los Cármenes. El club nazarí intentó renovarlo, pero sin alcanzar las condiciones ofrecidas desde Asturias. También aparecieron equipos dispuestos a pagar un pequeño traspaso en enero, aunque el jugador y su entorno prefirieron terminar la temporada y esperar al Oviedo. La apuesta está encontrando una respuesta inmediata. Con 25 años, Sáenz se ha convertido rápidamente en una pieza importante para Julián Calero. "Calero me pide que sea dañino en campo rival, en zona de tres cuartos. Siempre que llego ahí trato de hacer un pase agresivo o un tiro que pueda ser gol", explicó este miércoles tras recibir el reconocimiento como mejor futbolista de agosto. Y su inicio pone inevitablemente el foco sobre las condiciones del acuerdo. Pablo Sáenz tiene contrato hasta 2028, sin opción automática de ampliación, y una cláusula de rescisión de seis millones de euros mientras el Oviedo milite en Segunda División, que se duplica hasta los 12 millones en Primera. Su etapa como azul acaba de comenzar, pero el rendimiento ofrecido hasta ahora ya convierte su situación contractual en un asunto a tener en cuenta de cara al futuro.

articles.title: Premier League: What are the rules for academy players, and are they paid?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team looks at what rules players and clubs must follow when teenagers play in the Premier League
articles.body:
Premier League teenagers Max Dowman and JJ Gabriel have both made the headlines in recent days - for very different reasons.

Arsenal winger Dowman, 16, starred in their EFL Cup third-round win over Ipswich Town on Tuesday by scoring twice in a 4-2 win at Portman Road.

Dowman became the second-youngest player in Premier League history and the youngest player in Champions League history last season.

Meanwhile, highly rated Manchester United striker Gabriel, 15, has handed in a formal request to leave the club.

That is despite playing for the first-team during pre-season and being in line to make his official senior debut for Michael Carrick's side.

So what's it like for such young players balancing life, education and football?

Here is a look at the rules that they and their clubs must adhere to.

What is the minimum age for a senior appearance?

The minimum age for a senior appearance in the Premier League is the season or school year in which that player will turn 16.

In England and Wales school terms, it means that the player in question must be in year 11 before they can make a senior appearance.

For example, Arsenal winger Dowman made his first Premier League appearance at the start of last season as a 15-year-old as he was turning 16 later in the campaign.

Alongside Dowman, fellow wingers Ethan Nwaneri and Jeremy Monga also made their league debuts at the age of 15. Both were turning 16 later in that school year.

However, United forward Gabriel was not only allowed to make his senior debut last season. He could only do so this season, as he turns 16 next month.

In England, the academy system sees all participating clubs graded from Category 1 to Category 4.

Clubs in a higher category have the right to sign any player from a lower category for a structured compensation fee.

So Category 1, as the top category, can sign any player from a club in Category 2 to 4.

Youth players officially become contracted to a club when first signing a scholarship.

Prior to that, there are fewer rules binding them to a specific club - although a team will hold the player's registration rights if they have been registered for that particular season.

In order to play first-team football in the Premier League, that player must have a scholarship agreement with the club.

Players cannot be offered their first professional contracts until the season that they will turn 16. They cannot sign a professional contract until the day of their 17th birthday.

Upon signing a scholarship contract, youth players are paid a wage that is structured around an apprenticeship model.

Some youth footballers, that play for a club that is in a different country or part of the country than where their family is from, will be placed into accommodation with local families that work with that club to look after young footballers. They are often known as 'digs'.

For players not in digs and living at home with their own families, some clubs will give teenage players money to cover expenses such as accommodation and food.

It is common for many club academies to offer educational programmes for their academy players, in order to ensure that they are balancing football with academic studies and gaining valuable qualifications.

This is done in a number of ways. Some clubs put their own schools inside their club's academy training facilities, while others partner with local schools or have agreements with that player's existing school to balance educational work with football development.

A 2024 study from the University of Essex shows that just 4% of teenagers in professional academies go on to play top-flight football.

Because of that, clubs across the country ensure their players have more options with their career, should their hopes of making it as a professional footballer do not go to plan.

As well as studying core subjects such as English, maths and science, clubs have recently added further studies for their academy footballers that include life skills, media, financial education and driving lessons to set them up for whatever comes after their life as an academy player.

"We as clubs - with education, welfare - have got to make sure that those lads' academic potential is not hampered," Simon Ord, the former head of education at Derby County, told BBC Sport.

"It would be it ethically immoral if we just said 'okay you know you stay with us for four, five, six years. You can do as little as you want education wise', then we can't guarantee a professional contract, and then where's the kid?"

Some academy players are able to excel in both their education and on the pitch.

Ord, who has also worked in a similar capacity with England's youth sides, says that he personally limited how much schoolwork players missed out on during the year they took their GCSEs but said that it is possible to excel in both factors.

"To keep them coming out of school at 16, during that really, really important year, it's wrong," he says.

"Now there will be odd times, like the Max Dowmans and J.J. Gabriels of this world who are outliers, because they are top of the tree.

"But with Max Dowman, for instance. Max Dowman did his GCSEs and Arsenal have been absolutely brilliant amongst that, and he's come out with great grades. So you can do it."

For safeguarding purposes, players under the age of 18 are not allowed to get changed in the same dressing room as senior players, and therefore do so in an alternative changing area.

As part of that, clubs must ensure that youth players have a designated shower room that is monitored by an official chaperone such as a player liaison officer or a member of the club's safeguarding team.

For clubs with fewer members of staff in lower divisions, this can be other nominated staff members, providing they are DBS-registered.

Players younger than 18 years old are also not permitted to wear shirts that have gambling sponsors on them. This has recently become an easier issue for Premier League clubs to deal with, now that gambling sponsors are prohibited from being the front-of shirt-sponsor.

Other provisions, such as ensuring player safety in team transport and making sure they are not near alcohol when senior players are consuming it, are also considered.

Players under 18 are also exempt from the new 10 second sub rule, which requires players to leave the field at the nearest point. For safeguarding reasons, they should always leave at the half-way line by the dugouts.

articles.title: Lo nunca visto: 30.000 libras por una experiencia inmersiva como aficionado del Everton
articles.standfirst: Formará parte del partido benéfico #Game4Hope con leyendas del Everton y del Liverpool
articles.summary: Formará parte del partido benéfico #Game4Hope entre leyendas del Everton y el Liverpool
articles.body: El próximo 26 de septiembre tendrá lugar en el estadio del Everton el #Game4Hope con la presencia de leyendas del equipo local y del Liverpool. El objetivo será recaudar fondos para la comunidad local al tiempo que ayudará a combatir la falta de vivienda en Merseyside y la región. El partido pinta a un reencuentro épico. Peter Reid, leyenda del Everton, y John Barnes, su homónimo en el Liverpool, unirán fuerzas como entrenadores del equipo de Merseyside. Bajo sus órdenes, nombres como Leighton Baines, Gareth Barry, Phil Jagielka, Yakubu, Robbie Fowler, David James, Ryan Babel, Jari Litmanen, John Aldridge, Joleon Lescott y Louis Saha. Frente a ellos, un equipo del Resto del Mundo que contará con Cafú, Clarence Seedorf, Jaap Stam, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink o Mustapha Hadji. Pero partidos así hay varios cada temporada en diferentes puntos del mundo. La novedad que ofrece el Everton en su nuevo Hill Dickinson Stadium es una experiencia inmersiva que, para sus dos últimos tickets, está valorada en 30.000 libras. Por esa cantidad por persona, los invitados pueden alojarse en el hotel oficial del equipo, compartir comida con los jugadores, viajar con la plantilla e incluso entrenar con los equipos en la jornada de entrenamiento oficial del viernes. El paquete también incluye acceso a reuniones informativas previas del equipo y del entrenador, vivir desde dentro el ambiente previo al partido y la charla del entrenador... o incluso estar en el calentamiento con ellos. Posteriormente, pueden ocupar un lugar en el banquillo como miembros honorarios del equipo. Sobra decir que el paquete de 30.000 libras incluye la equipación personalizada, la camiseta firmada y el acceso VIP al partido. Posteriormente, al acabar el duelo y empezar la celebración... también tendrán acceso.

articles.title: David Gray: Hibernian sack head coach after six league games
articles.summary: Hibernian sack head coach David Gray six games into the Scottish Premiership season, ending the former captain's 12-year stay at Easter Road.
articles.body:
Hibernian have sacked head coach David Gray six games into the Scottish Premiership season, ending the former captain's 12-year stay at Easter Road.

Tuesday's 1-0 defeat by bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock leaves the Edinburgh club ninth in the table on six points.

It was Hibs' sixth successive home league loss, stretching back to last season.

Assistants Liam Craig and Craig Samson are also leaving, with John Potter placed in charge for Saturday's home game with Aberdeen.

"Ultimately, this is a decision that we have not taken lightly, but unfortunately, one as a board we had to make due to the recent downturn of results and performances," said executive chairman, Ian Gordon.

Gray famously led Hibs to Scottish Cup victory in 2016, heading in a stoppage-time winner against Rangers at Hampden to end a 114-year wait for a third success in the tournament.

Having signed two years previously, the right-back retired in 2021 after 177 appearances and joined the coaching staff.

Gray 'will continue until told otherwise' - but has Hibs boss lost the fans?

Struggling Kilmarnock condemn Hibs to sixth home loss in row

Latest Hibs news, analysis and fan views

After three shorts spells as interim manager, Gray took on the position of head coach in May 2024, replacing Nick Montgomery.

He won just one of his first 15 league games but the team staged a remarkable recovery to finish third, while Hibs were fifth last season.

Both campaigns yielded European qualifiers which ended in dramatic, last-gasp Conference League play-off exits.

Gray oversaw 107 games, winning 43, losing 35 and drawing 29. He departs with a League Cup semi-final against derby rivals Hearts to come on 1 November.

"Dave has been an inspirational figure at the club during his time here, and he has been a true friend and fantastic colleague to so many," added Gordon.

"On behalf of my family, I would like to personally thank him for everything he has done for us since we joined the club.

"As a person, he constantly set the standard with his attitude, professionalism and general work ethic and he will be sorely missed around the building by all the players and staff.

"On the pitch, he has delivered some incredible moments for our fans, and brought a level of stability and consistency that we haven't reached in recent years."

Darren : Sad to see Davey Gray go but correct decision. The writing has been on the wall for a long time. We need to be like Motherwell and Hearts and look outside of Scotland and find a manger with an exciting style of play and fresh ideas. No "old school" Scottish manager!

Robbie: It was a great run for David. But I think his time was up after the final whistle went last night. Not a great home run.

John: I would like to thank David for what he achieved for the club as a player and then coach with two decent seasons culminating in European football. The lack of drive, effort and leadership from the players this season has got him the sack. Good luck and thanks for May 2016.

Colin : It's a sad day. It felt inevitable after last night though. I wish David Gray all the best. I hope we take a modern approach to finding a new coach and don't go down the route of Malky's contact book

Callum: Unfortunately its all about results and we haven't achieved them with ultimately the highest paid squad in years i think the board need a trusted and experienced manager now.

Richard: David Gray is unfortunate - as he is only part of the issue. Malky Mackay [sporting director] should be sacked too - they are members of the same management team and bear equal responsibility.

Ben: We got lucky in the end with Gray. After a horrendous start he pulled it back and gave us a third place finish with back to back European qualification. The football and system played however has not been good enough. There is something sad about a club legend coming to thank the fans and instead getting booed, but there was no longer any positives to take, even for the happy clappers.

Sam : As a Hearts fan, I'm genuinely sorry to see David Gray sacked. He served Hibs well. I realise that he has to take the rap for the results, but the real truth is that at the moment his players simply aren't very good. These are lean times for Hibs, but they'll come again.

Josh: If Hibs could sack Pat Stanton and Frank Sauzee they were always going to sack a Scottish Cup winning David Gray. You see some of the dross in their back line and realise he had no chance of survival. Poor guy.

Alex: Sorry it came to that for David and wish him all the best, unfortunately the manager takes the hit. But the players have let him down time after time, clearly not good enough.

Keith: Truly gutted for Gray as the players need to have a long hard look at themselves. Simo Valakari from St Johnstone is the only manager other than Neil Lennon who we should be looking at. Big Marvin Bartley is for another time. All the best Sir David and thanks for all you've done for us over the years. I'll never forget the Scottish Cup win and the celebrations afterwards as long as I live.

Scott: Long overdue. This Hibs team is going back the way. It will take a miracle to get the best out off the dross we have. Need a manager that plays exciting attacking football. Tony Mowbry was the last manager that got me off my seat. It's been a while since I've been excited to watch Hibs.

John L: Neil Lennon or could the right offer be made to Alex Neil? Steve Clarke might fancy it. Stay away from Steven Pressley as he'll not go down well. Scandinavia seems to have good young coaches so perhaps there.

Ross: Wouldn't be adverse to Kevin Thomson, good motivator. I suspect Lennon will be favourite and that would not upset me one bit.

Ali: I'd like to see someone with zero connection to the club. Something a bit different from abroad. We have failed miserably over the last 10 years bringing British failures in. Time for a change.

articles.title: LSU Sack Leader Princewill Umanmielen Served in $550K Lawsuit Filed by Ole Miss
articles.summary: LSU sack leader Princewill Umanmielen has been served legal papers related to a July lawsuit filed by the University of Mississippi which alleges that the former Rebels edge rusher owes Ole Miss $550,000 because of his decision to transfer to the rival Tigers.
articles.body:
LSU sack leader Princewill Umanmielen has been served legal papers related to a July lawsuit filed by the University of Mississippi which alleges that the former Rebels edge rusher owes Ole Miss $550,000 because of his decision to transfer to the rival Tigers.

Records filed in Lafayette County Civil Court in Mississippi indicate that papers were served on Tuesday, just five days before No. 7 LSU was slated to visit No. 8 Ole Miss in a game immersed in hype stemming from coach Lane Kiffin's decision to leave Mississippi in favor of LSU last Nov. 30.

A person familiar with the situation said Umanmielen was served outside LSU's football operations complex. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because university officials have not commented publicly on the lawsuit between Ole Miss and two former players who are now at LSU, and who allegedly failed to compensate Ole Miss for their departure as required by revenue-sharing agreements they signed in early January.

The other is offensive lineman Devin Harper, who allegedly owes Ole Miss $400,000.

While legal issues between Ole Miss and Umanmielen have gone unresolved for months now, the timing of papers being served, first reported by ESPN, will only further pump up the intrigue surrounding Saturday night's game in Oxford, Mississippi.

It will mark the first time Kiffin has returned to Oxford since being showered with insults by angry Rebels fans as he arrived at a small airport to catch a private plane to Baton Rouge.

Kiffin persuaded four players and host of assistant coaches and other staff to follow him to LSU, including linebacker TJ Dottery and Winston Watkins Jr., Dottery is LSU's leading tackler through two games and Watkins Jr. leads LSU in yards receiving so far this season.

College athletes have been able to transfer far more freely in recent years without having to sit out a year, as was once required by the NCAA. There have been scattered disputes between players and their former schools over compensation agreements. Earlier this year, Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. said he would return to the Huskies after his school was reportedly prepared to pursue legal options to enforce his lucrative name, image and likeness contract.

Ole Miss has said revenue-sharing agreements signed by both players included a provision requiring them to compensate the university with a predetermined amount if they departed before fulfilling their commitment.

"The University of Mississippi has a responsibility to enforce its contractual terms, and this position is consistent with the actions of other institutions in the current landscape of college athletics," the Ole Miss statement said. "The university attempted to amicably resolve this matter prior to filing."

K iffin left Ole Miss following its regular-season finale against Mississippi State in late November. Kiffin initially asked to continue coaching the Rebels in the College Football Playoff after he'd accepted the position at LSU, but Ole Miss declined and appointed then-defensive coordinator Pete Golding as Kiffin's replacement. Golding coached Ole Miss to the national semifinals.

Umanmielen had nine sacks and 13 tackles for loss as a junior last season for the Rebels. Harper was a freshman reserve in 2025, appearing in six games.

articles.title: David Gray: Hibernian sack head coach with club ninth in Scottish Premiership after Kilmarnock defeat
articles.summary: Hibernian have parted ways with David Gray after defeat to Kilmarnock; Easter Road club have lost six consecutive league games at home for the first time since 1920; Scottish Cup winning captain Gray was appointed in June 2024 after fourth interim stint; Coach John Potter in interim charge
articles.body:
It follows a fourth league defeat in six games this season as Hibs lost to bottom side Kilmarnock on Tuesday .

Despite progressing to the League Cup semi-finals, Hibs were also knocked out of Europe after a Conference League play-off defeat to Gent.

Stretching back to last season, the Easter Road side have now lost six consecutive league games at home, equalling a club record last seen in 1920.

Gray was appointed on a permanent basis in June 2024, signing a three-year deal after his fourth stint in interim charge.

The 38-year-old, who retired from playing five years ago to focus on coaching, became a club legend when he scored the winner against Rangers in 2016 to end their 114-year wait to lift the Scottish Cup.

His start in the dugout was positive with a third-place finish in the 2024/25 campaign, while Hibs finished fifth last season.

However, with the team now two points off the bottom, the Easter Road hierarchy has decided it is time for change again.

Hibs are now searching for a sixth permanent boss in less than five years after the departures of Jack Ross in December 2021, Shaun Maloney five months later, Lee Johnson the year after, Nick Montgomery in the summer of May 2024 and now Gray.

Coach John Potter will take interim charge for Saturday's match against Aberdeen, with Hibs adding in a statement they "will announce a new permanent head coach in due course".

Gray sacked due to 'downturn of results and performances'

Hibernian executive chairman Ian Gordon said: "Dave has been an inspirational figure at the club during his time here, and he has been a true friend and fantastic colleague to so many at the football club. On behalf of my family, I would like to personally thank him for everything he has done for us since we joined the club.

"As a person, he constantly set the standard with his attitude, professionalism and general work ethic and he will be sorely missed around the building by all the players and staff.

"On the pitch, he has delivered some incredible moments for our fans, and brought a level of stability and consistency that we haven't reached in recent years.

"Ultimately, this is a decision that we have not taken lightly, but unfortunately, one as a board we had to make due to the recent downturn of results and performances."

Gray remained defiant following Tuesday's defeat against Kilmarnock, and speaking to Sky Sports following the game, he said:

"I've been here during difficult times and I've been here during good times and you can't just say it's brilliant when things are going well and then not expect a bit of criticism when things aren't.

"In terms of asking for patience, the fans are frustrated because we're not achieving what we need to be at this stage and winning enough games consistently, especially at home.

"And I accept that. All I can say is until someone tells me otherwise, I will be doing everything in my power, everything I possibly can as I have done at this football club to turn it around and I believe we can.

"It's a difficult time for everybody, the players, football club, because we've lost again off the back of a good result at the weekend and then failed to back it up again."

articles.title: Darian Mensah's Draft Stock 'Rising Like a Rocket,' NFL Scout Says amid Miami's 2-0 Start
articles.summary: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is making a strong impression on NFL talent evaluators to start the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is making a strong impression on NFL talent evaluators to start the 2026 season.

One scout told ESPN's Pete Thamel that Mensah "is rising like a rocket." Thamel added that the Hurricanes signal-caller is firmly in the Round 1 conversation for the 2027 NFL draft.

Mensah has thrown for 653 yards and eight touchdowns through Miami's first two games. He completed 41 of his 45 passes and averaged 14.5 yards per attempt.

The Hurricanes have yet to face a serious test. They opened the campaign on the road against Stanford and then hosted Florida A&M. Still, Mensah's volume and efficiency jump off the page.

The junior had already built a reputation for himself through his performance at Tulane and Duke in 2024 and 2025, respectively.

Mensah is the first quarterback off the board and No. 2 overall pick in Bleacher Report's mock draft .

"Mensah plays with immense poise and calmness in the pocket and during big games," the B/R Scouting Department said. "His ability to raise his level of play despite lacking premium talent at both Tulane and Duke displays his level of impact. Mensah plays with sound and clean mechanics, as well as the keen ability to layer passes down the field to his receiver in stride thanks to excellent ball placement."

There's going to be some serious competition in the upcoming QB class, a contrast from how Indiana's Fernando Mendoza was head and shoulders above the field in 2026. Oregon's Dante Moore could've been a first-rounder this past spring, and Arch Manning stabilized his stock with Texas' comeback against Ohio State in Week 2.

For right now, though, nobody has a lock on the top spot at the position. Much like Cam Ward in 2024, Mensah could claim that title if he continues his blistering start once the schedule gets tougher.

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England head coach defends controversial World Cup semi-final substitutions with Argentina adding: 'It's my scar, not yours'
articles.summary: England collapsed in the World Cup semi-final to lose 2-1 to Argentina and Thomas Tuchel has spoken about his in-game tactics for the first time since the tournament ended; Tuchel: "I'm in charge and I take these decisions. No-one is more hurt than me, no-one wanted it more."
articles.body:
England were 1-0 up and were five minutes plus stoppage time away from a first World Cup final since 1966.

But goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez turned the game on its head, after Tuchel had gone to a back five midway through the second half.

Tuchel - who made controversial comments about England's DNA after the semi-final loss - did admit that he may have played a defensive style of play too early in the semi-final.

But he also added that England's growing fatigue throughout the tournament and Argentina's crazy tactics meant he simply had to make those changes.

"You can try to kill me here. But it's my scar, it's not your scar," said the England manager, when reviewing the entire tournament in an England documentary.

"I have to live with it. It's not you having to live with this. I'm in charge here and I take these decisions.

"No-one is more hurt than me, no-one wanted it more. They can endlessly torture you and think: if I had done different substitutions, then we would have won the match. You just don't know it."

Read below for the England manager's views in full on how the Three Lions lost the World Cup...

Remember that huge Djed Spence tackle that kept England 1-0 up? That was the moment things started to change in Tuchel's head.

England had just led through Anthony Gordon and had two more chances to extend the lead through Declan Rice and Harry Kane. But an Argentina break saw Giuliano Simeone run through on goal, leaving Spence to make a last-ditch tackle.

Tuchel said: "We did quite well in the first half, it was totally an even match. We had good ball possession moments. I was actually happy and I saw us growing into this match. I felt we were there.

"From the start of the second half, I felt us on the back foot. I felt Argentina were more liberated and free in their movements, finding better solutions. Then we score, we have the next chance straight away.

"We go after them, we have a ball win, we have a chance, we have another half chance, we lose the ball in another attack and it's the Spence tackle and they almost score from a counter-attack.

"It did something to me, it maybe did something to the players. And we suddenly shift into a mindset of: 'let's just overcome it'. We played like there were four minutes left, rather than 30.

"From executions, the details of execution, playing around in deep build-up, playing around Messi, playing to one side then switching the side, bringing the game in the opponent's half, making them suffer, having time to recover physically and mentally in ball possession, we were lacking all these things."

Jordan Pickford produced a big save to deny Nicolas Gonzalez just before the final water break of the match. That prompted Tuchel to make a change. Off came goalscorer Gordon and defender Ezri Konsa arrived.

England were in the controversial back five.

Tuchel said: "Argentina then play very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, [they played] f*** it football. 'We have nothing to lose. Let's f*** it.'

"They played four strikers. They played two wingers, the two strikers and Messi. They took a No 6 off and put a No 10 in. A central defender off and played a No 6. At some points they played 3-1-6. And we struggled.

"A key moment if I look back at it and what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break. And I thought: we will not survive. This is waiting for death. We don't have ball possession, we're not defending good, we're not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.

"I wanted to give the players something: this is what we do. This is what we do now.

"Coming with this mindset and this experience, we ended the game against Norway in a back five. We ended the match against Mexico in a back five. And we did it. I thought Argentina relied heavily on crosses, they have four strikers in the last line. I think: let's play in a back five.

"I changed to a 5-3-2, we changed the structure. Because I believe we can handle the width better and we still have three central defenders in the middle if crosses still fly in. We changed then to a 5-4-1. Even my mindset is maybe like: let's just overcome it. And it's too early. Too early for that mindset."

And the pressure did not stop. Alexis Mac Allister struck the woodwork just after the break. England were under the cosh. The Argentina goals came shortly after.

'If we were better on the ball, I wouldn't have changed it'

Tuchel believes that the emotional toil of winning late on against DR Congo after trailing so long, then playing with 10 men in the Azteca altitude, then beating Norway in extra-time in the intense Miami heat played its part against Argentina.

Tuchel said: "It just piles up through the tournament. Congo, 70 minutes trailing 1-0, Mexico the altitude, flying to Miami and playing against Norway. We are tired. And still we hang on until the 88th minute."

Asked if could have made attacking subs instead, Tuchel added: "Of course you could. No-one knows what would have happened. We could have done it and maybe lost 2-1 and could have gone: 'Is he crazy? He finished the game against Norway with a back five, why didn't finish the game of with five?'

"I think from what I saw and the experience, the information and the level of craziness from Argentina put in - change after change after change, it was just one offensive change after the other. That was my solution to the problem.

"That's what the intervention of a coach is. I try to help, you don't implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.

"If we would have been more stable in the game, with more percentage of ball possession, I would have not changed the structure, why would I? And I would have gone for offensive changes. But that is a very, very difficult road to have gone down. That can torture you."

articles.title: Barcelona rising star seeks redemption with Spain after missing World Cup triumph
articles.summary: FC Barcelona attacking midfielder Fermin Lopez was forced to watch the World Cup from home when everything suggested he would play an important role in Luis...
articles.body:
FC Barcelona attacking midfielder Fermin Lopez was forced to watch the World Cup from home when everything suggested he would play an important role in Luis de la Fuente's Spain side.

A fracture to the fifth metatarsal in his right foot, suffered in May, required surgery and ruled him out of the tournament in North America, even as La Roja went on to lift the trophy.

Four months later, the picture has changed completely. Fermin is back at his best and has once again become one of the standout players in Hansi Flick's Barcelona side in the 2026/27 season.

His start to the season has been particularly impressive, with five goals and two assists in his first six appearances. Those numbers have quickly strengthened his case for a return to the national team, reports SPORT .

On Friday, De la Fuente will announce his Spain squad for the upcoming international break. And, unless there is a major surprise, Fermin is expected to be among those selected .

Fermin has made a brilliant start to the season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

From missing the World Cup to forcing his way back in

What happened in May was one of the toughest setbacks of the La Masia midfielder's young career. And his response on the pitch has been nothing short of emphatic.

Fermin returned at the start of the season and quickly rediscovered the form that had made him such an important player for Flick.

In the first game of the campaign, when Barcelona defeated Elche 5-0, Fermin scored twice, demonstrating his ability to make late runs into the box and find himself in scoring positions.

He followed that with goals against Athletic Club and Valencia . His contribution goes beyond the goals, however. He also provides creativity and the ability to break forward from midfield.

Friday's squad announcement could therefore carry particular significance for Fermin. It will mark his return to Spain's squad after missing the World Cup that his country ultimately won.

Redemption time. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Spain will begin their first Nations League campaign as world champions with a training camp starting on 22 September. Their schedule includes matches against England , Croatia and the Czech Republic.

And, Fermin wants to be there and establish himself as an important part of the team after the World Cup heartbreak.

articles.body: La Real y el Bournemouth se reencuentran en la Europa League después de haber sido en los últimos veranos rivales habituales en la pretemporada, ya que se han enfrentado en tres ocasiones, siempre en terreno británico, con un balance de una victoria txuriurdin y dos igualadas. En la preparación de 2025, por ejemplo, ambos equipos se midieron en dos choques jugados en dos días seguidos, para que todos los futbolistas tuvieran 90 minutos antes del arranque de la Premier y LaLiga, con un empate sin goles en el duelo más relevante, con Mikel Oyarzabal fallando un penalti, y un 1-1 en el que se disputó en la ciudad deportiva de los ingleses, tanto obra de Barrenetxea. Unos años antes, en 2022 el conjunto txuriurdin también visitó al que hoy será su oponente, en esta ocasión en el ecuador de la pretemporada y el triunfo, por 1-2, se vino para San Sebastián, con dianas de Mikel Merino e Igor Zubeldia. El partido de este jueves, por tanto, no será tanta novedad para los futbolistas de Real y Bournemouth, aunque los ahora dirigidos por Marco Rose podrán conocer Anoeta, después de las tres visitas anteriores de los guipuzcoanos. El hecho de que en juego estén los tres primeros puntos de esta fase Liga de la Europa League añade más competitividad a este habitual duelo amistoso.
